item.title: Shippable Governance and the Human in the Loop
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description: Over the past several months, I dove headfirst into the emerging practice of working with autonomous coding agents. In the broader cultural zeitgeist, people have started calling this “vibe coding”: describing a mode where you casually prompt a language model, lean back, and watch working software materialize on the screen.

item.title: Difference Needs Somewhere to Go
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description:
I was raised up believing I was somehow unique. Like a snowflake distinct among snowflakes. Unique in each way you’d conceive. And now after some thinking I’d say I’d rather be, a functioning cog in some great machinery, serving something beyond me.

Opening lyrics to Helplessness Blues by Fleet Foxes

item.title: Seeing the Difference Between a Boss and a Botanist
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description: In the sclerosis of corporate hierarchies, middle management often finds itself caricatured as a relic of bygone organizational structures, scar tissue left behind by the Peter Principle. From the bumbling inefficiency of Office Space’s Lumbergh to the clichéd “paper-pusher,” middle managers have been the subject of fascination, frustration, and ridicule. But these stereotypes belie a deeper truth: middle managers, especially in knowledge work are essential stewards of an organizations most important and undervalued resource: the team.

item.title: From Shovels to Software: Why Difference Matters When Things Get Complex
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description:
In many creative activities the medium of execution is intractable. Lumber splits; paints smear; electrical circuits ring. These physical limitations of the medium constrain the ideas that may be expressed, and they also create unexpected difficulties in the implementation.

Implementation, then, takes time and sweat both because of the physical media and because of the inadequacies of the underlying ideas. We tend to blame the physical media for most of our implementation difficulties; for the media are not “ours” in the way the ideas are, and our pride colors our judgment.

- “The Mythical Man Month” — Fred Brooks, 1975

item.title: Building a Trade-off Mentality
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description:
If you wish to make an apple pie from scratch, you must first invent the universe.
– Carl Sagan

Carl Sagan’s famous quote inspires deeper thought of how connected our universe is, that to “make an apple pie from scratch” you can keep going one step backwards until one has to “invent the universe.” What struck me was, that somewhere between the start of the universe and baking the pie, we had to draw a line for what we consider “from scratch.” Why would buying pre-made pie crust feel like “cheating,” yet buying pre-ground flour would not? What lines have we drawn without much thought of how we choose them?

item.title: Changing Requirements to be a Successful Business Analyst
item.author: liam@atlancia.com (Liam Shaw)
item.description:
A look into personal experience with business analysis, agile and modern projects.

My first exposure to the business analyst role was at the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), while working with a team focused on policy. While there, I was fortunate enough to involve myself in other initiatives, giving me exposure to a new world of roles within the organization.
